Subject: Post-call: PoC scope & cost/latency tradeoffs (batching vs streaming)

Thanks Anna & Tom — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways (from today's demo + discovery)
- Primary use case: clinical summarization + extraction for provider notes.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~60M tokens/month; peak bursts up to ~150M tokens/month (EOD batch windows).
- Latency requirement: two flows — interactive/EHR lookup (p95 target < 250ms) and nightly batch summarization (throughput prioritized).
- Security: data stays in your VPC for the PoC (Private deployment option on the table).

Cost / unit-econ ask
- You asked for target unit cost guidance and an initial budget band. For qualification, please confirm whether your target $/1M tokens is closer to $800, $1,000, or $1,200 — that drives tiering and whether Dedicated capacity makes sense.

Our immediate proposal
1) 3-month PoC: focus on two flows (streaming-enabled interactive + batch pipeline).
2) Pilot config: streaming for interactive (low  latency, higher cost), batching for nightly (cost-optimized).
3) Deliverables: redwood_poc_cost_model.xlsx (attached), PoC checklist & mutual action plan.

Action items for Ava Health
- Confirm steady vs peak token split and a target $/1M tokens band.
- Share a short sample prompt distribution (avg input tokens / avg output tokens).

Next steps (mine)
- I'll send an updated cost model with explicit price bands for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private along with expected p95/p99 latency impacts by config.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min pricing & procurement sync on Wed Nov 4.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC scope & cost/latency tradeoffs (batching vs streaming) — price bands + tradeoffs

Appreciate the detail, Anna — that's exactly what we need. High-level pricing and engineering tradeoffs below (I kept numbers conservative until we lock volume bands).

Unit economics (indicative) — $ / 1M tokens
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $1,600 / 1M (streaming enabled), $1,100 / 1M (batch-optimized)
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 6-mo commit): $850–$1,100 / 1M depending on commit level and burst allowance
- Private (on-prem / VPC): pricing by negotiation; typically similar to Dedicated with additional infra fee

Latency vs cost tradeoffs
- Streaming (low tail latency): best p95 for interactive flows but higher cost due to less batching opportunity and increased resource reservation. Recommended for UI path where p95 < 250ms is required.
- Aggressive batching: dramatically reduces unit cost (up to ~40% savings) for high-throughput jobs but increases tail latency; good for nightly summarization.
- Hybrid: streaming for <300ms p95 routes + batching for bulk jobs is the most cost-effective PoC approach.

SLO-driven pricing examples (for planning)
- Standard SLO (p95 < 500ms): $1,200 / 1M
- Low-latency SLO (p95 < 250ms): $1,700 / 1M
- Premium SLO (p95 < 150ms, <50ms baseline): $2,300 / 1M

Notes on optimization levers
- KV/prefix cache can reduce prompt tokens by ~10–30% for repetitive contexts.
- Mixed-precision quantization & model variant routing can cut per-token compute cost but may affect quality.
- Autoscaling policies with burst credits can keep latency stable during short peaks while keeping committed capacity lower.

Attachments: updated_cost_model_v2.xlsx (contains banded pricing & example bills for 60M/150M scenarios).

If those numbers look close, our recommended next steps:
1) You confirm steady vs peak split + sample prompts (Anna).
2) Redwood prepares a 3-month PoC quote with two routes (Standard stream + Batch heavy) and a mutual action plan; legal & procurement ops get the DocuSign MSA for a pilot.
3) Intro call between Ava eng and our infra lead (Evelyn) to validate caching assumptions and tail behavior.

I'm free Wed Nov 4 at 3pm PT for a quick pricing sync.

—Marissa
